final_report.question: Assess stock status and environmental drivers of European hake in FAO 37.2, 2010-2020

plan.question: Assess stock status and environmental drivers of European hake in FAO 37.2, 2010-2020

sub_questions.text: What is the landings/catch trend over the period?
What is the current stock status vs reference points?
Are environmental covariates associated with the stock metrics?

plan.rationale: Parsed deterministically from the question text.

claims.text: This report addresses: Assess stock status and environmental drivers of European hake in FAO 37.2, 2010-2020. It synthesizes 7 quantitative results and 2 references. All numeric claims are grounded in the cited source records.

Trends were tested with the Mann-Kendall test and Theil-Sen slope; stock status was classified against MSY reference points (Kobe quadrants); covariate associations used lagged cross-correlation of linearly detrended series, with p-values based on an autocorrelation-adjusted effective sample size (Pyper & Peterman 1998) and Bonferroni-adjusted over the lags tested. All statistics are computed by deterministic, unit-tested functions; associations are not causal.
Landings show a decreasing trend (Mann-Kendall p=2.62e-05; Theil-Sen slope -495.9 tonnes/yr, 95% CI [-544.4, -455.7]).
Spawning stock biomass shows a decreasing trend (Mann-Kendall p=5.16e-05; Theil-Sen slope -959.8/yr).
As of 2020, Merluccius merluccius in 37.2 is classified 'both': biomass below B_MSY and F above F_MSY.

No significant association between SST and landings after detrending; the strongest lag is with SST lagging landings by 4 yr (detrended r=0.44, Bonferroni-adjusted p=1). Associational only - not causal. Both series linearly detrended before correlating (raw r=-0.83). Best lag selected post hoc over 9 lags; reported p uses an autocorrelation-adjusted effective sample size (N*=5.7 of n=7) and is Bonferroni-adjusted (×9).

No significant association between SST and SSB after detrending; the strongest lag is with SST lagging SSB by 3 yr (detrended r=-0.28, Bonferroni-adjusted p=1). Associational only - not causal. Both series linearly detrended before correlating (raw r=-0.90). Best lag selected post hoc over 9 lags; reported p uses an autocorrelation-adjusted effective sample size (N*=6.3 of n=8) and is Bonferroni-adjusted (×9).

No significant association between CHLOR_A and landings after detrending; the strongest lag is with CHLOR_A lagging landings by 4 yr (detrended r=-0.48, Bonferroni-adjusted p=1). Associational only - not causal. Both series linearly detrended before correlating (raw r=0.56). Best lag selected post hoc over 9 lags; reported p uses an autocorrelation-adjusted effective sample size (N*=7.0 of n=7) and is Bonferroni-adjusted (×9).

No significant association between CHLOR_A and SSB after detrending; the strongest lag is with CHLOR_A leading SSB by 4 yr (detrended r=-0.54, Bonferroni-adjusted p=1). Associational only - not causal. Both series linearly detrended before correlating (raw r=0.55). Best lag selected post hoc over 9 lags; reported p uses an autocorrelation-adjusted effective sample size (N*=7.0 of n=7) and is Bonferroni-adjusted (×9).
The literature includes "Stock status and warming-linked distribution shifts of European hake in the central Mediterranean" (2019), relevant to these findings.
The literature includes "Mediterranean sea surface temperature trends 2000–2020 and implications for demersal fisheries" (2021), relevant to these findings.
Landings trend in 37.2: only 11 years, so Mann-Kendall has low power to detect a trend.
SSB trend in 37.2: only 11 years, so Mann-Kendall has low power to detect a trend.
Stock status in 37.2 is based on the terminal assessment year (2020) only, with no uncertainty on B/B_MSY or F/F_MSY.
SST vs landings in 37.2: the raw correlation (r=-0.83) reverses sign after detrending (r=0.44), so it reflects shared trends, not year-to-year co-variation.
SST vs landings in 37.2: only 7 aligned years, and the lag was picked after the fact, so the test has low power and the best lag is unstable.
SST vs SSB in 37.2: the raw correlation (r=-0.90) is not significant after detrending (adjusted p=1), so it mostly reflects shared trends.
SST vs SSB in 37.2: only 8 aligned years, and the lag was picked after the fact, so the test has low power and the best lag is unstable.
CHLOR_A vs landings in 37.2: the raw correlation (r=0.56) reverses sign after detrending (r=-0.48), so it reflects shared trends, not year-to-year co-variation.
CHLOR_A vs landings in 37.2: only 7 aligned years, and the lag was picked after the fact, so the test has low power and the best lag is unstable.
CHLOR_A vs SSB in 37.2: the raw correlation (r=0.55) reverses sign after detrending (r=-0.54), so it reflects shared trends, not year-to-year co-variation.
CHLOR_A vs SSB in 37.2: only 7 aligned years, and the lag was picked after the fact, so the test has low power and the best lag is unstable.
